testcase.title: ACL-permitted local user can authenticate during quiet-mode

source_facts.claim: The report says the valid local login from an ACL-permitted host is rejected during quiet-mode after failed attempts.
The original report describes Telnet and three failed attempts; the later manual verification uses SSH and a 3-attempt/60-second configuration.
The bug record includes historical fix verification on NX-OS 10.6(3) build 10.6(2)IMG9(0.152), and it also notes the original fix had been in 9.3.1.

TaskLog records Normal-Mode after successful login; it does not establish quiet-mode persistence after login.

source_facts.claim: The release note describes authentication/accounting reaching ISE while an authorization request does not; conditions include mgmt0 down and an inband route/server source interface.
The Unit-test notes show mgmt0 down, Vlan150 up, inband Telnet login and `show user-account` roles; the comments label the role result as evidence the authorization packet was sent successfully.
The record says Cisco lab reproduction was not consistent, while the later verification comments identify a fix verification build and link a historical automation archive.

The exact transport is Telnet in the historical transcript; equivalent remote login transport may be used if it causes the same authorization flow.

testcase.title: Directed-request rejects overlength VRF input without device denial of service

source_facts.claim: The security release note says crafted login input with directed-request enabled can cause an unexpected device reload due to incorrect input validation.
The RCA says the VRF-name in the directed-request username format can exceed the maximum length of 32 characters, causing stack corruption; fix adds validation and a syslog.
The unit-test notes configure directed-request and show failed malformed login attempts and AAA_VRF_LENGTH_EXCEED messages; the terminal capture obscures the exact input string.
The RCA reports unit coverage for valid/invalid credentials with directed and non-directed modes; protocol scope includes TACACS+ and RADIUS.

requirements.description: Evidence proves an approved VRF-name exceeding the report’s 32-character limit was submitted while directed-request was enabled.
The invalid attempt is rejected and the DUT remains responsive with no reload/crash or related new core.
A subsequent valid remote authentication succeeds; claim TACACS+ and RADIUS separately.

reported_behavior.observed_incorrect_behavior: With directed-request enabled, a crafted login string containing an overlength VRF-name can corrupt the stack and cause an unexpected device reload (DoS).

sources.finding: The archived run UIDs are included in the active aggregator job.

Quiet-mode trigger activates/verifies quiet mode, checks non-permitted denial, then checks permitted login success; after-login state is a separate observation.
LoginBlockTest is parameterized for SSH/Telnet and local/remote AAA; it does not implement supervisor OIR or directed-request malformed input.
OpenConfig case creates and validates server-group configuration via NETCONF; it is not an XML-agent show/tacacs-server state-read test.
Flexi SSH uses inband target addresses and tests authentication variants; this section does not assert mgmt0-down, ISE authorization receipt, or returned roles.
Standalone Flexi job runs the SSH/SCP/SFTP/reload variants; no bug-specific CSCvz55570 claim is inferred from its name.
